kinematics.blade_normal: the paddle body's local +x axis (the face normal); the handle runs along its local +z
kinematics.rule: world pose of a body = parent pose x translate(pos_in_parent) x rotate(quat_in_parent_wxyz); a body with a hinge joint then rotates by the joint angle q about joint_axis_in_body (through joint_pos_in_body); the base body's two slide joints translate it by base_x along its x axis and base_y along its y axis (so the base sits at (base_x, base_y, 0) in your frame). The parent of the base is the world (your frame).

arm.robot: Franka Emika Panda (FER): the manufacturer's joint limits (Franka 'Control Interface Specification and Robot Limits'; bodies/franka_panda/body.toml)

base.note: per axis; speed 2 m/s (a belt-driven linear gantry, as DeepMind's table-tennis robot), acceleration 8 m/s^2 (the drives' force limit for the moving mass), jerk 200 m/s^3 (an estimate: no manufacturer value)

limits.checks: a traj is refused (400) if two consecutive rows differ by more than max_target_step or three consecutive rows have a second difference beyond max_target_second_difference (= the acceleration limit x (10 ms)^2); the first row used is rejected if it does so with the target in force (and its velocity, zero if the rows start later). Jerk is not checked: the servo smooths it

controller.law: at 1 kHz; the reference r interpolates linearly from the previous target to the new one over the 10 ms step, its velocity rd = their difference / 10 ms. A setpoint generator follows (r, rd) and never exceeds the speed (the arm's at 0.9 of its limits), acceleration and jerk limits (the arm's jerk also capped by its torque-rate limit at the pose: 0.7 x 1000 N m/s / the row sums of the arm's inertia matrix); a reference beyond them is followed late. Arm: tau = M qdd_sp + kp (q_sp - q) + kd (qd_sp - qd) + gravity/Coriolis, then limited to 87 / 12 N m and 1000 N m/s of change (1 N m per ms); a joint pushed more than resync_rad from its setpoint makes the setpoint follow it. Velocity reflex: an arm joint faster than 1.05 x its velocity limit stops the robot - the targets are ignored and the setpoints brake to rest at the pose of the trigger - for 1 s, then it resumes from rest (servo.reflex, servo.n_reflex); the collision reflex does the same when the robot's links or paddle press on the table with more than 20 N (servo.n_collision_reflex). Base: force = kp (b_sp - b) + kd (bd_sp - bd) + bias, clipped at force_limit_n

limits.units: base_x, base_y in m, m/s, m/s^2, m/s^3; q1..q7 in rad, rad/s, rad/s^2, rad/s^3

deliverable.allowed: numpy, scipy, mujoco, the toolkit under /opt/robot (robot_only.xml, assets, lib/tt_kinematics.py, lib/tt_servo.py) and files inside /app/output/skill; module-level memory between calls of one run; state = the low level's observe state (no images, no ball coordinates), spec = game spec's kinematics, limits, toolkit, skill_contract; no network, no other files, no other processes
optional: step(*, state, spec) -> a command or None (called every 20 ms between hits: the return to a ready pose, the base's position)
deliverable.signature: hit(t, pos, normal, vel, *, state, spec) -> one low-level command ({'type': 'traj', 'k0', 'q': rows of 9 targets} | {'type': 'slew', 'q', 'speed'} | {'type': 'hold'}) or None; the contact at control step state['step'] + round(t / 0.01) (in the API test the command takes effect at state['step']; in the match when your call returns, spec timing)

skill_contract.feasible: every API-test request comes from our reference player's own matches (L1-L4) on this revision and is feasible under the real limits: from the case's start state the platform's implementation plans it and its own rehearsal (the robot alone) delivers it within 15 mm, 2.5 degrees and 0.10 m/s + 8 % (IK residual < 1 mm, no table contact, the base in time); a request that asked for more paddle speed than the limits allow carries the velocity scaled the way the platform's skill scales it
skill_contract.measured: the blade centre (site paddle_center), its face normal (the paddle body's +x) and its linear velocity in the simulator's state at the contact step k_c = k_eff + round(t / 0.01) (as the high level's act: its reply's n_swing_steps_available); time_err_s = the step of the blade's closest pass to pos within +-0.1 s, minus k_c (x 10 ms); the case starts from the exact state of one of our reference player's matches (the robot as the match left it, the ball in flight) and runs to the leg's verdict, step() called every 2 control steps

notes.authority: the implementation reads only the robot's own state and its commands, never the ball or the opponent: it executes the paddle state it is asked for and neither predicts nor aims (P2). The high level's rehearsals roll the robot alone (no ball) on a copy of the simulator; the low level's toolkit gives the same robot-only model and servo law
notes.ball: the measurement also reports whether the ball went back (ball_returned; not part of success)
notes.failure: a request outside the ranges: refused (400, nothing changes); a contact time already passed: 'too late', no stroke (high level) / no command; not enough time or speed: the best reachable contact, the reply says how much (speed_scale, blade_error_m); a low-level command beyond the limits: refused, the previous command goes on and the hit fails the API test; the skill raising or overrunning its time limit: no command (counted), after a time-out no further calls in that run
notes.feedback: high level: the act reply (stroke: ok or what limited it, blade_error_m, normal_error_deg, speed_scale, the base goal); low level: the robot's own observed state after every step
notes.frame: your frame: x to your right, y towards the opponent, z up; table top z = 0
notes.inputs: t, pos, normal, vel as above; the implementation also gets state (the low level's observe state: the robot's own joints q, qd, the target in force q_target and its velocity qd_target, the command in force, base_xy, paddle_pos / paddle_normal, step; no images, no ball coordinates) and spec (game spec's kinematics, limits, toolkit, skill_contract)
notes.refused: a command refused by the low level's checks (joint ranges, speed and acceleration limits, continuity of the first row) fails the hit; so does the robot touching the net (robot_net_contact: a lost point by the rules). Touching the table is allowed by the rules since revision 9/7 (D4) and is reported (robot_table_contact), not a failure: the table stops the paddle, which already shows in the tolerances
notes.timing: the command a hit returns takes effect at control step state['step'] (k_eff); contact at k_eff + round(t / 0.01); a hit with t below the time the robot needs is answered as well as it can be (no refusal); a new hit replaces the stroke under way; between hits step() may move the robot (every 20 ms). In the match (the skill in the loop) the call's compute counts: the world runs on while hit computes and its command takes effect at the first control step after it returns (spec timing); the contact stays at state['step'] + round(t / 0.01) and the rows of a traj that have passed are skipped

skill_contract.replaces: a new hit replaces the stroke under way (as the high level's act): plan from the robot's current state (q, qd, q_target, qd_target, the command in force)

normal.doc: blade face normal at contact (non-zero; pointing at the opponent)

pos.doc: blade centre at contact (m, your frame): |x| <= 2.0, -3.3 <= y <= -0.3, -0.5 <= z <= 1.5

t.doc: time from the hit's effect until contact, 0 < t <= 2.5

skill_contract.returns: one low-level command of this level (game spec actions: {'type': 'traj', 'k0', 'q': rows of 9 targets [base_x, base_y, q1..q7]} | {'type': 'slew', 'q', 'speed'} | {'type': 'hold'}) or None, taking effect at control step state['step'] (that is k_eff); the high level's implementation lowers the act to the same traj command. The base is part of the skill: the implementation moves it (the high level: the stance rule, rcb_tt.stance)
skill_contract.success: every tolerance met and no refused, no robot_net_contact

tolerances.text: blade centre within 2 cm of pos at the contact step
face normal within 3 degrees of normal
closest pass to pos within 10 ms (one control step)

ik_library.algorithm: damped least squares on MuJoCo's own Jacobians (mj_jacSite) of the robot-only model: blade centre position + face normal (roll free), full rotation, or position only, the base held at a given position; joint ranges by clipping; solve_near: q_ref and 12 fixed starts, the accurate solution with the least speed-weighted travel. The rail: the slew's documented go-to law and the high level's documented stance rule
api: solve(pos, normal=None, R=None, q0=None, base=(bx, by), ...) -> (q_arm7, err)
solve_near(pos, normal=None, R=None, q_ref=None, base=(bx, by), vel_limit=None, ...) -> (q_arm7, err)
base_goto(b, v, goal, a) -> (b, v, a)
base_plan(b, v, goal, n, a) -> (rows, arrived)
ik_library.use: import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '/opt/robot/lib'); from tt_kinematics import PaddleKinematics

not_provided: hit: our implementation, the high level's act {t, pos, normal, vel} (the paddle state at contact) - the player implements hit itself
the stroke planner: match.Match.plan_paddle / _ik_best, rally.stroke_rows and bodies/trajopt.py (the limits-aware swing, timing, rehearsals, speed scaling), the duel's plan worker

servo_model.algorithm: the robot's own servo law exactly as game spec limits.controller documents it (the simulator's rcb_tt.TTServo: JerkLimiter + torque-rate limiter for the arm, the rail's jerk-limited setpoint), at 1 kHz on the robot-only model: the same motion as the robot without contacts with the world (tests: test_exploit_toolkit_is_the_manifest replays rows bit for bit)
api: RobotSim.rollout(rows) -> per row (blade pos, normal, vel, q, qd)
servo_model.use: import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '/opt/robot/lib'); from tt_servo import RobotSim

toolkit.yours_to_develop: hit(t, pos, normal, vel): where the base stands, the swing trajectory (joint targets over time within the real limits) that delivers the requested paddle state at the requested time, paddle speed and face control at contact, the ready pose, compensating the servo's lag, re-planning when a new hit replaces the stroke under way
